evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The start page lists title, date and time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingList.tsx:32-42, format.ts:3, start.jpg), and each card has a 'Book <title>' link (TastingList.tsx:46-48). The form has the labels Name, Email and Guests, a 1-8 limit and a 'Book' button (BookingForm.tsx:103-123, shared/schema.ts:17-21). The server never takes more seats than are left (store.ts:70-74). Errors appear next to their field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows 'Booking confirmed' with the tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.tsx:26-33, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.tsx:64-70, server/index.ts:6). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, plus a Cancel button that frees the seats (Staff.tsx:103-131, store.ts:90, staff.jpg). The app is React with Express, React Router, react-hook-form and zod, runs with npm start on PORT (default 3000), keeps bookings in memory and is in English. The fully booked state (8-list-desktop.png) and the phone layout (6-staff-phone.png) are both present.
evidence.correctness: Booking is synchronous, so the seat check and the insert cannot interleave (store.ts:52-85), and api.test.ts:85-95 proves it with two simultaneous requests for the last 5 seats. When seats are short the error says exactly how many are left, with correct singular and plural (store.ts:71-74). Cancel deletes the booking and the seat count is recomputed from the remaining bookings, so cancelled seats are freed. A second cancel returns 404 (staff-api.test.ts:104-113). The schema checks type, integer, the 1-8 range, whitespace-only names, length limits and trimmed emails (schema.ts). The form's default guest count is capped at the seats left (BookingForm.tsx:61,70). Bodies over 10 KB get 413 and malformed JSON gets 400 instead of 500 (app.ts:50,108-111). Minor gap: if the logout request fails, onSignOut throws an unhandled rejection (Staff.tsx:31-34).
evidence.security: The password is compared with timingSafeEqual on SHA-256 digests, so lengths always match (auth.ts:3,19). If no password is set, sign-in is disabled (auth.ts:18). The session token is 32 random bytes in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie that is Secure when the request is secure, and it expires on the server after 12 hours (auth.ts:21-22, app.ts:85). The login limiter counts only failed attempts (app.ts:40-47). Helmet sets the CSP and other headers. Staff routes check the session with requireStaff. The public booking summary leaves out personal data (app.ts:73-79). React escapes output, and staff.test.tsx:95-101 tests that HTML in a name renders as text. No secrets are in the code.
evidence.code_quality: The code is small and well separated: shared zod schema, store, auth, routes, pages. Store and auth are factories with injectable clock and options, so they are easy to test. Error handling is explicit, with typed results such as BookResult. Naming is clear. Nits: staffSession in api.ts:46 is exported but never used, and the client imports types from server/store (api.ts:2).
evidence.tests: Store tests cover seat accounting, the exact-capacity boundary, cancel and unique references. API tests (supertest) cover 10 invalid-input cases, 413 and 400 responses, concurrency, over-capacity booking and the PII-free summary. Staff API tests cover login, the throttle, session expiry, protected routes, cancel and logout. UI tests run the real React app against the real Express server and check labels, errors linked through aria-describedby, the server's seat error, the fully booked state, the confirmation, staff grouping and cancel, the expired-session path and XSS. Static serving has its own tests (spa.test.ts), and a Playwright e2e script asserts there is no horizontal scroll on a phone (e2e/run.mjs:29).
evidence.ux_design: The design is warm and coherent: wine and gold colours, serif headings, cards with date badges (start.jpg). Error states are clear, with a red-tinted field and an icon (form.jpg). Success is clear, with a green check and a details box (confirmation.jpg). Fully booked tastings are greyed out with a badge (8-list-desktop.png). Weak points: dates are shown as raw '2026-11-06 18:00' strings, there is no imagery or description of what each tasting includes, and staff Cancel deletes a booking at once with no confirmation or undo (Staff.tsx:126-127).
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked to their inputs. Inputs have aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing to the error or hint (BookingForm.tsx:89-114). Focus moves to the first field with a server error (BookingForm.tsx:83). Loading text uses role=status, and the actions column header is screen-reader only. The date badge is aria-hidden so it is not announced twice. Focus outlines are visible gold, and the muted and green text pass contrast checks. On phones, table rows become labelled cells. Gaps: every row's button has the same accessible name, 'Cancel', with no booking context, and each field error has its own role=alert, so several alerts fire at once.
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies match the task: Express, React, React Router, react-hook-form with zod, plus helmet, express-rate-limit and cookie. The source is about 700 lines. Some hardening, such as TRUST_PROXY parsing and the session TTL options, goes slightly beyond what a three-tasting winery app needs, but it is not bloated.
evidence.maintainability: The README explains install, build and start, STAFF_PASSWORD, TRUST_PROXY, the in-memory store, where tastings are defined, the test and e2e commands, the code layout and an API table. There is a lockfile and a strong regression suite. Missing: no CI pipeline, no ADRs or specs explaining decisions, no staff manual, no release or versioning approach beyond version 1.0.0, no .nvmrc (engines is just '>=22'), and dependencies use caret ranges. dist/ and dist-server/ were delivered even though .gitignore excludes them.
evidence.visual_design: The palette, type pairing, rounded cards, pill buttons and spacing are consistent across all four screenshots and look finished. The header has a gold rule and the brand mark repeats in the favicon. The look is still fairly generic: no photography or wine imagery, and the ISO date strings next to the date badge feel repetitive (start.jpg, form.jpg).
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear: hero heading, then a three-card grid with the CTA at the bottom of each card (start.jpg). Form and confirmation sit in a centred panel (form.jpg, confirmation.jpg). Staff bookings are grouped in a panel per tasting with tables, and the phone view stacks into labelled rows (staff.jpg, 6-staff-phone.png). No overlap, clipping or overflow was seen, and e2e/run.mjs:29 asserts there is no horizontal scroll.
evidence.usability: A guest books in two steps: Book link, then a three-field form. The guest count is pre-filled and there is a back link. Errors appear inline next to the field and the Book button is disabled while submitting. The confirmation can be reloaded. Staff sign in once and stay signed in, and the empty state says 'No bookings yet.' Friction: Cancel has no confirmation, so one mis-tap deletes a guest's booking for good, and the dates are hard to scan.
evidence.reception: Guests would see a trustworthy, professional winery booking page with a clear confirmation and reference, and staff get a clean list. It lacks winery character (photos, tasting descriptions, contact or location details) and friendly date formatting, so it reads as polished but plain.

strengths: Correct, race-safe seat accounting with server-side zod validation shared with the client, backed by strong store, API, real-server UI and e2e tests (store.ts:52-85, api.test.ts:85-95, tests/ui/*).

Solid security for its size: timing-safe password check, random HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session tokens with server-side expiry, login throttling, helmet, and a public booking summary with no personal data (auth.ts, app.ts).
Coherent, polished winery look with clear error, success and fully booked states that works on a phone (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, 8-list-desktop.png, 6-staff-phone.png).
issues: Staff Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation or undo, and every row's button has the same accessible name, 'Cancel' (Staff.tsx:126-127), so one mis-tap loses a guest's booking for good.
Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no ADRs or specs, no staff manual or versioning approach, no .nvmrc, caret dependency ranges, and build output delivered despite .gitignore.

Dates are shown as raw '2026-11-06 18:00' strings, and there are no tasting descriptions, imagery or contact details, so the site reads as plain rather than as a winery's own site (start.jpg, confirmation.jpg).
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, fully compliant booking app: correct seat limits, solid staff authentication, thorough tests and a coherent, mobile-friendly winery design. It could ship after a confirmation step for staff Cancel, friendlier date formatting and basic CI and project documentation.
